EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
Nida Experiment Card PC130 - 52A
SCRs are used in DC and AC circuits. In this lesson, you will learn about the operation of a SCR in a DC circuit.
INTRODUCTIONM
DC SCR circuits are called trigger circuits................
The SCR controls the application of power to the load, it is an electronic ON/OFF switch that uses current to operate.
Let's begin the lesson on SCR TRIGGER CIRCUIT OPERATION...................
LESSON MENU
SCR TRIGGER CIRCUIT
This is a typical SCR trigger circuit......................
DISCUSSION
The purpose of the circuit is to apply power to the load resistor RL, using the SCR as a switch.
The SCR has an input circuit that applies gate current (Ig) which turns it ON.
+DC forward biases the SCR. When the SCR is ON, anode current (Ia) flows through the load.
In this trigger circuit, which component/components comprise the input circuit?
R1 is not in the input circuit. R1 is part of the reset circuit that turns the SCR OFF.
TRY AGAIN!
R1, C1 and S1 make up the reset circuit. They are not part of the input circuit. The reset circuit turns OFF the SCR.
TRY AGAIN!
In this trigger circuit, which component/components comprise the reset circuit?
R1 is in the reset circuit. However, R1 does not turn OFF the SCR by itself, there are other components.
TRY AGAIN!
TRY AGAIN!
ircuit which is used to turn the SCR ON.
R2 is not in the reset circuit. R2 is in the input circuit which is used to turn the SCR ON.
The operation of a trigger circuit is based on two independent currents, Ig and Ia.
Applying a positive voltage to the input circuit establishes gate current flow.
Ig causes the gate semiconductor material (P Type) to vanish.
Ig causes the gate semiconductor material (P Type) to vanish.

P MATERIAL GATE - The gate is made of a thin piece of P material between two pieces of N material. Current flow from the cathode to the gate causes the two N materials to combine, this eliminates the effect of the P material.....................................................................................................................................................................

P MATERIAL GATE - The gate is made of a thin piece of P material between two pieces of N material. Current flow from the gate to the cathode causes the two N materials to combine, this eliminates the effect of the P material......................................................................................................................................................................
With +DC supplying forward bias,the SCR turns ON producing Ia.
The SCR turned ON which supplied power to the load. Ia flows through RL.
One note, if Ia is small, the SCR will immediately turn back OFF.
A small Ia allows the gate's P material to reform, blocking cathode to anode current flow.
A small Ia allows the gate's P material to reform, blocking anode to cathode current flow.
A small Ia allows the gate's P material to reform, blocking cathode to anode current flow.
A small Ia allows the gate's P material is reform blocking anode to cathode current flow.

P MATERIAL GATE - The current flowing through the SCR will keep the P material gate from reforming. However, if Ia is too small, there is not enough electrons to fill the holes and P material reappears stopping current flow.

P MATERIAL GATE - The current flowing through the SCR will keep the P material gate from reforming. However, if Ia is too small, there is not enough negative charges to attract the positive charges and the P material reappears stopping current flow.
The minimum Ia required to sustain current flow is called HOLDING CURRENT(Ih) and is given in transistor reference books.
To turn OFF the SCR, the reset circuitis used. Reset circuits either stop Ia or reduce Ia to less than Ih.
With S1 open, the left hand plate of C1 has +DC voltage on it. C1 prevents this steady voltage from reaching the anode of SCR 1.
Closing S1 places a ground on the left hand plate of C1. This drops the voltage from +DC to 0 V.
The change in voltage is coupled across C1 momentarily placing a ground on the anode of SCR 1.
The ground on the anode of SCR 1 reverse biases the SCR interrupting current flow. The SCR turns OFF.
With SCR 1 OFF, power is no longer applied to the load.
With S1 open the circuit is back to its initial state. When an input is applied to the gate, the SCR turns ON and supplies power to the load.
Which current flow is applied to the load when the SCR turns ON?
Ig is the current that turns the SCR ON. It is independent of the current that flows through the load.
TRY AGAIN!
Ih is the term used to describe the minimum Ia current required to hold the SCR ON.
TRY AGAIN!
If Ig is applied to the gate and Ia drops below Ih, what happens to the SCR?

choices.label: The SCR turns ON and stays ON
The SCR turns ON and then OFFDD

text: The SCR does not turn ON and stay ON. With Ia less than the holding current, Ih, the SCR turns ON but, the current flow through the SCR can not keep the SCR ON.
TRY AGAIN!
The SCR does not stay OFF. Applying gate current to the SCR and having the SCR forward biased will turn the SCR ON. Because Ia drops below Ih, the SCR turns back OFF.
TRY AGAIN!
This completes the information on SCR TRIGGER CIRCUIT......

2. The input is applied to the gate. Ig is developed which will allow the SCR to turn ON...
3. With the SCR forward biased, the SCR turns ON. If Ia is larger than Ih, the SCR remains ON..
4. The reset circuit turns the SCR OFF. S1 reverse biases SCR 1 interrupting anode current flow....
